thread:
maya: heads up — ran a short drill on preemptible GPU surges in us-west2, logging notes here. noticed a 2-3s spike in pod evictions when az B hit capacity limits.
omar: nice, can you drop the commands you used to repro? we'll add them to the SOP.
maya: sure — quick repro steps i used (run in test cluster):
```
# create eviction-heavy batch
kubectl apply -f test-preemptible-job.yaml --namespace=spot-drill
watch -n1 'kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep preemptible'
```
note: test-preemptible-job just spins GPUs at ~95% mem to trigger scheduler reshuffles.
lee: were evictions graceful? any SIGTERM window issues?
maya: most pods got the default 30s SIGTERM. two jobs failed to checkpoint because they didn't handle SIGTERM. adding lifecycle hooks fixed those.
sophie: thumbs up. we should standardize preemption hooks: exit code handling + atomic checkpoints. add example code snippet for model-serving containers.
maya: example lifecycle for python worker:
```
trap "python /app/checkpoint.py && exit 0" TERM
# main serve loop
python /app/serve.py
```
this ensures a fast checkpoint before process exits.
omar: good. ops question: when AZ shows >80% preemptible churn, what's the immediate mitigation? (we need an explicit, short runbook top-of-page)
lee: mitigation trio: 1) scale up ondemand pool (fallback), 2) route low-priority traffic to smaller models, 3) enable burst queue to buffer requests. do we have quick kubectl / infra CLI commands for 1)?
maya: yes — for autoscaling ondemand group (gke example):
```
# increase node pool size
gcloud container clusters resize my-cluster --node-pool=ondemand-pool --num-nodes=6 --zone=us-west2-b
# or helm patch to increase dedicated-capacity replicas
kubectl scale deploy/dedicated-gpu --replicas=4 -n infra
```
infra-bot: detected node_preemptions in us-west2-b: 24 events in last 5m. average reclaim time 2.8s.
sophie: infra-bot alert is great, but add an escalation level: page infra-sre if >50 events in 10m or >10% sustained error rate on serving routes.
omar: agreed. propose escalation path:
- pager to oncall (primary infra) immediately if infra-bot threshold breached
- if oncall can't restore in 15m, escalate to infra lead (lee)
- >60m and customer impact: exec-alert and customer-success heads.
maya: i'll add thresholds and runbook steps. also a short checklist for oncall to run in first 10m:
1) check infra-bot alerts and node events
2) verify autoscaler status and pending node count
3) temporarily scale ondemand/dedicated pools
4) enable model degradation route (traffic-split to smaller model)
5) capture diagnostics (kubectl get events, pod logs, dmesg)

lee: for diagnostics, add a one-liner bundle command we can paste in pager channel:
```
kubectl -n spot-drill get nodes -o wide; kubectl -n spot-drill get pods -o json > /tmp/spot-pods.json; journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager | tail -n200 > /tmp/kubelet.log
```
this reduces chatter.
sophie: also include cost-impact guidance: if we sustain >30% ondemand fallback for >2h, trigger cost-review with finance and throttle non-critical batch jobs.
maya: added. final thing — best practice: always run a small warm pool of ondemand nodes in each region (1-2 nodes) so we can warm kernels and avoid cold start slowdowns when we scale. note: warms should be autoscaler-protected with taints + tolerations for only warm jobs.
omar: can we automate warm pool recreation on AZ imbalance? maybe a controller that observes preemption rate and flips on a warm-pool flag.
lee: good follow-up. for now, manual steps in the SOP are fine. i'll own the controller RFC.
maya: wrapping up — i'll push the short SOP to the infra runbooks repo and schedule a 15m drill next week to validate paging and the checklist.
sophie: :thumbsup: schedule and invite rotation oncall.
infra-bot: reminder set: drill on 2026-03-23 16:00 UTC.
